jp: 社員[しゃいん]{は|wa-topic}田中[たなか]さん{と|to-and}山田[やまだ]さん、二人[ふたり]だけです。
en: The staff are just Mr. Tanaka and Mr. Yamada, only two people.
why: The two names are the complete list, so と is needed; や would suggest more people.

jp: 同僚[どうりょう]{と|to-and}私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}どちらも新入社員[しんにゅうしゃいん]です。
en: My colleague and I are both new employees.
why: どちらも (both) needs the complete-list と; か would mean one or the other.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{と|to-and}数学[すうがく]、両方[りょうほう]あります。
en: There is homework in both English and math.
why: 両方 (both) requires と, which joins exactly these two subjects.

jp: この学校[がっこう]{に|ni-location}{は|wa-contrast}アメリカ{と|to-and}中国[ちゅうごく]、両方[りょうほう]{の|no-possessive}留学生[りゅうがくせい]{が|ga-existence}います。
en: This school has students from both America and China.
why: 両方 (both) needs と for the complete pair; か would mean one or the other.

jp: 休[やす]み{の|no-possessive}日[ひ]{は|wa-topic}宿題[しゅくだい]{や|ya-list}掃除[そうじ]{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}します。
en: On days off I do things like homework and cleaning.
why: Homework and cleaning are examples among other chores, so や (with など) lists them.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]{で|de-place}田中[たなか]さん{や|ya-list}山田[やまだ]さん{など|nado-etc}{が|ga-subject}意見[いけん]{を|o-object}言[い]いました。
en: At the meeting, people like Mr. Tanaka and Mr. Yamada gave their opinions.
why: The two names are only examples and など shows there were others, so や is right.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]{の|no-possessive}あと、図書館[としょかん]{で|de-place}宿題[しゅくだい]{や|ya-list}予習[よしゅう]{など|nado-etc}{を|o-object}します。
en: After class I do things like homework and preparation at the library.
why: Homework and preparation are examples of what I do, so the open-list や fits with など.

jp: 英語[えいご]{か|ka-or}フランス語[ご]、どちら{か|ka-indefinite}{を|o-object}選[えら]んでください。
en: Please choose either English or French.
why: Choosing one of two options takes か; と or や would list both and clash with どちらか (either).

jp: 質問[しつもん]{は|wa-topic}メール{か|ka-or}電話[でんわ]、どちら{でも|demo-any}かまいません。
en: For questions, either email or phone is fine.
why: The two ways are alternatives, so か is used; と or や cannot go with どちらでも (either).

jp: 社員[しゃいん]{は|wa-topic}昼[ひる]{に|ni-time}カレー{か|ka-or}ラーメン、どちら{か|ka-indefinite}{を|o-object}食[た]べられます。
en: At lunch, employees can eat either curry or ramen.
why: The employee picks one of the two dishes, so か marks the alternatives; と or や would mean both.
